# Loomle

Loomle is an agent-native Unreal Engine integration. It turns complex editor
state into SAL, the Structured Agent Language: compact ordered text that people
and agents can read, copy, query, and patch without replacing UE's native
object model.

Canonical user documentation:

- Home: https://loomle.ai/
- Install: https://loomle.ai/install.html
- Quickstart: https://loomle.ai/quickstart.html
- Core concepts: https://loomle.ai/concepts/
- MCP calls: https://loomle.ai/calls/
- Agent Skill call: https://loomle.ai/calls/agent-skill.html
- Interfaces: https://loomle.ai/tools/
- Workflows: https://loomle.ai/workflows/
- Blueprint formatting workflow:
  https://loomle.ai/workflows/blueprint-format-graph.html
- Source: https://github.com/loomle/loomle

Availability and installation:

- The latest stable Loomle release is available from GitHub Releases:
  https://github.com/loomle/loomle/releases/latest
- Supported engine versions are Unreal Engine 5.7 and 5.8. Supported native
  targets are Apple Silicon macOS (`darwin-arm64`) and x64 Windows
  (`win32-x64`).
- Choose the complete archive matching the installed engine version. Each
  includes native binaries and self-contained Clients for both platforms.
- Stable download URLs:
  https://github.com/loomle/loomle/releases/latest/download/loomle-bridge-ue5.7.zip
  https://github.com/loomle/loomle/releases/latest/download/loomle-bridge-ue5.8.zip
- Fab provides the current marketplace-approved build. GitHub Releases may
  publish a newer engine-specific package while a Fab update is under review:
  https://www.fab.com/listings/f0fb545c-b1d9-4525-8642-3f170134c428
- The plugin contains the Bridge and self-contained Client at
  `Resources/Loomle/<platform-arch>/loomle(.exe)`.
- No website installer, Python, uv, Node.js, global Loomle install, separate
  project Client, host-specific Skill installation, or session-attachment
  daemon is required.
- When upgrading from 0.6, close Unreal Editor and remove or move the old
  `<Project>/Plugins/LoomleBridge` out of every affected project's `Plugins`
  directory. A project plugin shadows the engine plugin.

Eight public MCP tools:

- `status({})`: report Client/update status and bound session/Bridge health.
- `project`: inspect projects and bind one MCP session to one project.
- `sal_query({ text })`: execute one self-contained SAL Query Text.
- `sal_patch({ text })`: dry-run or apply one ordered SAL Patch Text.
- `sal_schema({})`: return the active interface-module index.
- `sal_schema({ module })`: return one static interface card.
- `agent_skill({})`: list resident Loomle workflow Skills and their trigger
  descriptions.
- `agent_skill({ name })`: load one exact resident Skill and all of its
  Markdown guidance.
- `editor({})`: return the current UE interaction target as canonical SAL
  Result Text.
- `editor({ operation: "open" | "close", target })`: idempotently open, focus,
  or close one exact Blueprint Editor or Graph document using a bare canonical
  SAL Target expression.
- `python({ operation: "run", script })`: run Unreal Editor Python only when no
  structured Loomle interface covers the required capability.
- `python({ operation: "poll", executionId })`: follow only the exact
  continuation returned by a running Python execution; never replay the script.

The Python fallback has no SAL dry run, transactional rollback, safe
cancellation, or idempotency. Prefer a structured Loomle interface whenever
one covers the task.

MCP-managed Agent Skills:

- The `agent_skill` tool description exposes resident Skill names and trigger
  descriptions to the model automatically.
- When a task matches a Skill, the agent should load that exact Skill before
  planning the specialized workflow.
- `use-unreal-python` supplies the general safety, API discovery, idempotency,
  recovery, persistence, and verification workflow for every Python fallback.
- `debug-unreal-pie-with-python` starts, inspects, exercises, and stops an
  in-process PIE session after the general Python Skill is loaded.
- `format-unreal-blueprints` formats and audits Blueprint K2 graphs using live
  node bounds and pin geometry.
- Skills guide use of existing Loomle tools. They grant no capabilities and
  have no separate install, update, or configuration lifecycle.

Six active SAL interfaces:

- Asset
- Blueprint
- Class
- Graph
- StateTree
- Widget

Recommended workflow:

1. Call `status({})` once.
2. If the task matches a resident Skill, load it before planning.
3. Bind one project when the session is unbound.
4. Locate the exact flat Domain Target.
5. Query a compact view.
6. Discover static or dynamic schema only when needed.
7. Use a UE Palette capability before creation.
8. Dry-run the complete Patch.
9. Apply the same authored Patch and read back.
10. Compile and save through the owning asset.

Every Query or Patch declares one flat
`target { domain: asset|blueprint|class|graph|state_tree|widget, ... }`.
Contained objects use Target-relative `@identity/path` references; kind words
never form part of identity. Ordinary objects use `{...}`. Optional semantic
tags are erasable presentation metadata and never select a Domain or type.
Public results begin with `result exact_target`, `result domain_root`, or
`result unresolved_target`; mutation metadata and diagnostics are later,
independent MCP text blocks.

Do not guess UE Classes, fields, Pins, object ids, destinations, Palette
entries, or operation names. The Client's `sal_schema` interface cards and
exact `with schema` results are authoritative for the installed build.
